final_answer:
MEMORANDUM. To: M. Calloway. From: J. Reeves. Re: Prescott Whitman redline (June 2, 2025) of Silverpeak/Ridgeway Transfer Agreement (Cascade Growth Fund III) - Redline Analysis. Benchmarks: our clean draft; Playbook v3.2 (PB); LPA excerpts (Hargrove & Sitwell).

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

1. Do not sign June 6 on this paper. Four changes can independently defeat GP consent or breach the LPA, and a GP denial is effectively fatal: a denial or deemed denial (LPA 9.3(b)) bars resubmission for 90 days, so a mid-July denial runs to about mid-October, past the September 15 Outside Closing Date.
 (a) ERISA rep deleted (new 5.7 "[Reserved]").
 (b) Interim "Voting Direction" covenant (new 5.8).
 (c) Affiliate-assignment proviso (10.4) stripped of the Eligible Transferee condition.
 (d) Open-ended price mechanics (new 2.5 true-up) that change the "terms" the GP's ROFR and consent are based on.
2. The redline is NOT a reliable comparison. Its unmarked base text is a different document from our clean draft (restructured and renumbered). Its header says May 20 (you say May 22), and I count roughly 30 tracked groups versus your 47. Substantive changes were made WITHOUT tracking (Part III). Run our own full compare, and demand a true redline against our draft, before any concession.
3. Playbook breaches requiring Managing Partner (David Koehler) WRITTEN approval (PB 1, 11): holdback 20%/270 days; cap removed; ERISA deletion; non-compete; New York law; courts instead of JAMS. Oral approval is not recognized. Recommendation: reject or counter all; no concessions without David's signed approval.
4. Financial headline: closing cash falls $3,551,200 (-11.1%) to $28,409,600; $7,102,400 held 270 days; indemnity uncapped; one-way true-up and a new capital-call indemnity add further uncapped Seller exposure.
5. Timeline issue in our own draft: LPA 11.2(b) lets the GP defer consent until the 15-Business-Day ROFR runs (about July 8 if the notice is delivered June 13). Consent in July therefore yields an Effective Date of October 1 under our definition (first day of the quarter after consent) - after the September 15 outside date. July 1 is realistic only if the GP acts by June 30. Fix: confirm with Hargrove whether quarter-start is LPA-required; if not, redefine Effective Date or extend the outside date.

II. MATERIAL DEVIATIONS (priority; section; analysis; response)

CRITICAL (reject / substantially revise)

1. ERISA rep deleted (5.7). Our draft 3.2(h) had a full rep, including no prohibited transaction. LPA 9.2(a) requires transferee ERISA/plan-asset representations; 9.5(a)(iv) bars transfers that cause plan assets; 9.5(c) makes failure to deliver requested ERISA reps grounds for denial; Eligible Transferee clause (c) excludes Benefit Plan Investors unless the GP determines otherwise; PB 8.1 calls the rep "non-negotiable" and "transaction-stopping" (MP escalation). Under 29 C.F.R. 2510.3-101(f), plan assets arise when Benefit Plan Investors hold 25% or more of any class of equity. Deletion also signals Ridgeway may be, or hold, plan assets: ask Prescott directly. Response: REJECT; reinstate our 3.2(h) verbatim; require a Buyer ERISA/BPI certificate with the Transfer Notice and a covenant to supply the GP's requested look-through data. Also conform the "Eligible Transferee" definition to LPA (ERISA prong (c) and GP-imposed requirements (d); both drafts omit them), and add the PB 8.1(d)-(e) Buyer reps (no registration; no publicly traded partnership), which neither draft has.

2. Interim Voting Direction (5.8). Seller must vote "solely as directed" by Buyer; failure is a "material breach." LPA "Transfer" expressly includes any transfer of "voting or economic rights ... whether or not ... record ownership" changes. This is an unconsented partial Transfer, void under 9.1, breaches our own LPA-compliance rep (4.6) and PB 5.2. Response: REJECT. Fallback: information-only covenant (existing 7.5(d)) plus a non-binding statement that Seller may consider Buyer's views, in Seller's sole discretion.

3. Non-competition (7.9; "Competing Fund" definition). Three years; bars Seller and Affiliates from acquiring any interest in any fund of the GP or any growth equity fund above $500M (Fund III itself is $1.15B, so the definition sweeps in most of the market); Buyer-only injunction and stipulated irreparable harm. PB 7: reject outright, no exceptions, MP escalation. The new severability clause (10.7) invites a court to rewrite it narrower, and the GP will see the covenant in the Transfer Notice. Response: REJECT in full, delete the definition. No fallback offered; any trade requires David's written approval.

4. Indemnity cap deleted (6.3(a)). PB 4.1: 15% maximum = $5,326,800 (and the cap should apply to fundamental reps, with fraud only excluded). Redline: unlimited, so theoretical exposure up to the entire $35.5M and beyond. Our own draft 6.4(c) exempted Fundamental Representations from cap and basket, which already exceeds PB 4.1; this needs David's written sign-off or correction before we reply (raise on Friday). Response: REJECT; restore 15% cap (Seller aggregate, all claims other than fraud).

5. Post-closing true-up (2.5; Adjusted NAV; Northbridge). The Purchase Price reduces dollar for dollar by any shortfall of "Adjusted NAV" at the Effective Date, determined by a Buyer-selected firm in Buyer's "reasonable discretion," final absent manifest error, one-way (no upside), no cap, shortfall payable by Seller within 10 Business Days. PB 2.1-2.2 bars buyer-selected valuers and discretionary methodology; only administrator/audited NAV is acceptable. Our 2.2 said the price was fixed with no true-up; that sentence was silently deleted. Flaws: (i) double counting: the 2.4(b) distribution adjustment already cuts the price, and distributions also lower NAV; (ii) dollar-for-dollar on NAV although the price was 92% of NAV: a 5% NAV decline = $1,930,000 (5.4% of price), 10% = $3,860,000; the $7,102,400 holdback is exhausted at an 18.4% decline; (iii) mismatch with LPA 11.2(d): a price reduction after the ROFR waiver, or terms not disclosed in the Transfer Notice, require a new notice and a new ROFR period. Response: REJECT. If a true-up must exist (PB 2.2): audited Fund financials only, calculated within 30 days of the next audit, symmetric, capped, with a default resolution, and written approval before offering. Prefer a modest price concession as the trade.

6. Holdback 20% / 270 days (Art. I, 2.3, 6.4). PB 2.3 maximum is 10% and 120 days, in escrow with a third-party agent. Redline: $7,102,400 (+$3,551,200, 100% over limit), 270 days (+150 days, +125%), 7.1M exceeds the playbook cap by $1,775,600 (133% of the $5,326,800 cap), so it is unjustifiable as security. Silently also: the escrow was deleted and Buyer "retains" the funds (PB 2.3: "under no circumstances" held by buyer), and interim-period adjustments and the true-up are netted against it. Response: REJECT; restore 10%/120 days, Escrow Agent, closing-date settlement of 2.4 adjustments.

7. Unfunded Commitment Indemnity (6.5). Seller indemnifies Losses from GP capital calls in 12 months above $2,500,000, with no basket, 18-month survival, and applying even to "increase in capital commitments." Maximum on the existing commitment: $3,825,000 - $2,500,000 = $1,325,000 (35% of the unfunded amount); increases uncapped. PB 4.3(a),(c) bars it (beyond the 60-day tail, one-sided); it re-prices risk the Buyer assumed by taking the $3.825M commitment, whose calls fund assets that increase NAV. Under LPA 9.4 Seller's exposure is a 60-day joint-and-several tail, ending when the transferee posts a letter of credit or cash equal to the unfunded amount. Response: REJECT. Restore our deleted 7.5 (Buyer posts 9.4(b) security and indemnifies Seller for tail calls) and 7.2; offer only a flat rep that called/unfunded amounts are accurate.

8. Basket now first-dollar (6.3(b)). PB 4.2 forbids it. Basket $355,120; at $500,000 of Losses, recovery rises from $144,880 to $500,000 (+$355,120, always equal to the basket once exceeded). The redline also limits the basket to 6.1(a) claims and expressly exempts 6.5. Response: REJECT; restore deductible. Describe it by operation ("liable only for Losses in excess of") and not by the label "tipping," which in market usage often means first-dollar.

9. Dispute resolution (10.2-10.3). Governing law Delaware to New York; JAMS arbitration to exclusive Manhattan courts; jury waiver deleted. PB 9 and 11: all three need MP approval; no court forum without a mutual jury waiver. Loses confidentiality and arbitrator expertise; exposes Seller to a jury. The LPA is Delaware-governed (15.1); split law adds risk. NY enforces a NY choice of law for contracts of $250,000 or more (GOL 5-1401) and forum clauses at $1M or more (5-1402) (from memory; not verified, egress blocked). Response: REJECT. Fallback needing David's approval: Delaware law with NY seat; if courts are unavoidable, mutual jury waiver plus Commercial Division and confidentiality.

SIGNIFICANT (negotiate)

10. Survival (6.3(c)). General 12 to 36 months (+24 months, 3x the PB limit); Fundamental to "statute of limitations plus 60 days" (about six years plus under New York law, CPLR 213(2), unverified, versus PB 24 months). PB 3.2 bars both. Also, "No Broker" was silently added to Fundamental Representations. Response: counter 12/24 months; Fundamental definition back to authority, title, no liens (and due authorization); covenants survive per terms.

11. Post-closing cooperation (7.8). 60 days to 18 months (+480 days, 9x); 40 hours per quarter (up to about 240 hours); tax, accounting and "investor communications"; $25,000 out-of-pocket cap deleted. PB 6: 60 days, $25,000, no personnel commitments, no investor-meeting support. Response: counter with our 7.4 (60 days, $25,000, Buyer reimburses excess in 15 Business Days). Any extension (e.g. 90 days for tax information) needs partner approval.

12. Affiliate assignment (10.4). Eligible Transferee condition (b) dropped, "does not delay" added. A change of transferee after ROFR waiver requires a new notice and ROFR period (11.2(d)), and GP consent runs to a named Buyer. Response: counter: assignment only before the Transfer Notice or with GP written consent; Affiliate must be an Eligible Transferee with ERISA reps.

13. Silent MAE and closing-condition expansions (8.1). Our MAE: since Signing, on the Interest or Seller's ability to close. Redline: since the March 31 Reference Date (pre-signing), on "value, condition, or prospects" of the Fund portfolio, a walk right on any market move. Seller deliverable of GP consent "reasonably satisfactory to Buyer" (3.2(c)). Seller to deliver a joinder (3.2(b)): wrong, the LPA 9.2(b) joinder is the transferee's. Written-waiver ROFR alternative deleted from 8.1(b). Response: reject; restore ours.

14. New Seller indemnities and reps, untracked. 6.1(c) pre-Effective Date taxes of "the Fund", and 6.1(d) ownership-related third-party claims, both uncapped; flat 4.6 "paid all capital calls" and numbers (ours were knowledge-qualified); Seller PTP rep (4.8) that belongs to Buyer. Response: strike (c)-(d) or limit to Seller-level taxes; restore knowledge; move the PTP rep to the Buyer (PB 8.1(e)). Cite Code 1446(f), not 1445, for partnership-interest withholding (W-9; unverified).

MINOR / ADMINISTRATIVE (accept or tidy)

15. Silently deleted protections to restore: mitigation (6.4(e)); claims procedures (6.5); mutual specific performance (10.9); Buyer regulatory covenant (5.6); post-closing distribution/call mechanics (7.6); notice/certificate exhibits. 
16. Tracked administrative: email notice (10.1(d)) accept with real addresses (Schedule A blank); Business Day redefinition (align to LPA); severability (10.7) once 7.9 is removed. Verify addresses (410 vs 400 Park).

III. LPA/REGULATORY FLAGS AND ACTIONS

GP-denial grounds (sole and absolute discretion, 9.1; no fiduciary duties, 15.7): items 1, 2, 12, 5, plus the Transfer Notice itself, which must disclose actual terms (irrevocable ROFR offer, 11.2(a)). Securities Act/PTP: a single 7.8% transfer should fit the Treasury Reg. 1.7704-1(e) block-transfer safe harbor (over 2% of capital; from memory, unverified); multiple assignments (item 12) erode that comfort. 9.1(a)/9.5(c) opinions at Seller's cost and 9.6 fee (to $50,000) must be budgeted.

Data discrepancies: (i) LPA dated January 15, 2017 in the excerpts but October 15, 2017 in our draft; (ii) Schedule A shows a $45M commitment as "7.8%," yet $45M of $1.15B is about 3.9%; get an Arrowpoint capital-account statement before Seller makes any rep on percentage.

Friday strategy: (1) confirm David is not being asked for the six MP approvals; (2) return our draft with a short must-have list (ERISA, no voting direction, no non-compete, 15% cap, deductible basket, no true-up, 10%/120 escrow); (3) trade only within the playbook (cooperation to 90 days with partner approval, notice mechanics, MAE refinement); (4) pre-clear ERISA/Eligible Transferee status and ROFR waiver with Hargrove and the GP; (5) do not sign until Transfer Notice terms are final, since later material changes restart the ROFR (11.2(d)).
